newsitem.title: USA: Merrill Lynch in deal with NYC to keep jobs. [CORRECTED 17:18 GMT]
newsitem.headline: Merrill Lynch in deal with NYC to keep jobs. [CORRECTED 17:18 GMT]

text.p: Merrill Lynch said Friday (corrects from Tuesday) that it agreed to expand its facilites in New York City and create 2,000 new jobs there, in exchange for a package of incentives worth $27.6 million over the next 15 years.

The package, neogotiated over three months, includes $17 million in sales tax exemptions if Merrill maintains its current city workforce of 9,000, plus an additional $10.6 million if Merrill creates the additional 2,000 jobs, the city's Economic Development Corporation said.

The brokerage said it will also buy a 700,000-square-foot office building at 222 Broadway near its lower Manhattan headquarters in order to consolidate and expand offices scattered throughout the city.

A source familiar with the talks, however, said that while Merrill Lynch had considered moving some workers to New Jersey, it had never considered moving its headquarters from Manhattan, as the EDC maintained in an announcement of the package.

The source also said that the 2,000 jobs added over the next 15 years, many of them technical, would be only a small part of the company's projected job growth over that time. Merrill, said the source, is expected to do substantial hiring internationally, to support its technological infrastructure, and in some of its retail operations over the same period of time.

The source said Merrill will probably also expand its workforce in New Jersey, where it now has 9,000 workers throughout the state, working in jobs ranging from back office processing to customer service, to mutual fund management.
The most likely site would be in the Plainsboro N.J. area, where the company is looking to consolidate several of its facilties.
New Jersey and New York have conducted frequent "border wars" in past years, as each state sought to lure corporate jobs with packages of tax incentives.
